title: Dependency Plan v1 (dependency-plan-v1)
description: Structural contract for the Baseline Repair Agent's inferred pip requirements, asked of the model when a third-party research repository ships no requirements file. What is checked: the two fields the prompt's output shape declares — a packages array and a notes string — because the runner feeds packages to pip as argv and prints notes to the researcher. What is deliberately NOT checked here: that each spec is a bare distribution name with optional version clauses (no flags, URLs, local paths, `-e`, `-r`, comments or shell metacharacters) — that grammar is a security boundary and lives in validateRequirementSpec (src/comparison/dep-inference.ts:50), which drops offending entries with a visible reason instead of failing the plan; nor the MAX_PACKAGES bound or the notes truncation in parseDependencyPlan. No pattern and no maxItems: a list the platform can sanitize must not be rejected wholesale, and over-many specs are truncated rather than aborted. Enforcement point, so the next reader does not move it: assertAgainstSchema runs at the END of parseDependencyPlan on the repaired plan, never on the model's raw answer. `notes` is required of that plan (a shipped plan always carries one) although the model may omit it, because the parser turns an absent or non-string note into '' plus the refused-spec stamp; requiring it of the raw answer would abort plans that work today — tests/dep-inference.test.ts feeds exactly such an answer — and a repaired field is not a contract the producer must satisfy.

packages.description: Bare pip requirement specs, e.g. "torch", "numpy>=1.21,<2". Grammar-checked one by one; only strings that pass become install args.

notes.description: What the evidence showed and which specs were refused. The parser also stamps rejected-spec counts here, so an empty or absent value is repaired, not rejected.
